title: Term lexicon
description: A registry of the corpus's terms of art: one entry per headword, its original-language forms, and the English renderings it travels under. The lexicon is retrieval apparatus, not evidence. It says what to search for and where a rendering was seen; it never says what a text claims. Nothing here may be cited by an extraction unit or a synthesis output - those may quote only a commentary.

sources.description: Where renderings come from. Every rendering names one of these, so a reader can tell an attested pairing from an imported one.

kind.description: 'commentary-corpus' is the only kind a script can verify: the pairing is stated in a commentary, so the rendering carries a locator and scripts/synthesis_lexicon.py --check looks it up. 'dictionary' is a published reference work, 'translation' a named translator's standing rendering, 'registry' a term already asserted elsewhere in this repo. The last three are unverifiable by construction and are marked so rather than blended in.

citation.description: A bibliographic reference or repo path. Never the source's own text: see docs/lexicon-design.md L4.

id.description: Transliterated headword slug (leib, koerper, fuersorge). One entry per term of art, not per author: a term shared by several authors lists them in 'authors' rather than being duplicated.

headword.description: The term as its own language writes it.

authors.description: Author folder names whose commentaries use this as a term of art. Restricts --attest and --candidates; not an assertion that no one else uses it.

forms.description: Inflectional and orthographic variants, the headword included. These are searched with the same left-anchored, deliberately over-inclusive matcher the themes use.

theme.description: Theme id from synthesis/themes.json. Optional: an entry with no theme is a candidate, and that is what --candidates ranks.

ordinary_english.description: Forms a search cannot separate from ordinary English, so --expand never proposes them as search terms. Two causes, both measurable with --attest: a homograph, where the German is spelled like a common English word (Not, Interpretation, Situation), and a prefix, where the left-anchored matcher fires inside longer English words (Natur in 'nature', Tod in 'today', Irre in 'irreducible'). The forms stay in 'forms' because they are the term's real forms; this is the German-side counterpart of the absent_terms rule in synthesis/CLAUDE.md.

contrast_with.description: Entry ids this term must not be collapsed into (Leib/Korper, Zeitlichkeit/Temporalitat). The pairing is what makes a shared English rendering a finding rather than a coincidence.

gloss.description: An aid to recognizing the term in a search result, in the registrar's own words. Never evidence, never a definition copied from a reference work, and never citable downstream.

english.description: An English form this term travels under in the commentaries. Feeds themes.json search_terms via --expand; a rendering that is wrong costs a glance on a candidate list, a rendering that is missing costs a whole commentary.

source.description: Source id from the top-level sources array.

translator.description: Whose standing rendering this is, where the divergence is a translator's (Macquarrie-Robinson vs. Stambaugh) rather than an author's.

locator.description: commentary-slug#section-id where a commentary itself states the pairing. Required when the named source is of kind 'commentary-corpus', and checked: --check confirms the section contains both the English and one of the entry's forms.
